title: Pressure: Force on an Area
summary: Pressure = force ÷ area. Why knives are sharp, why camels have wide feet, and why nails have points.

ib.note: Pressure in pascals (N/m²) is used in MYP 4–5

cbse.chapter: Curiosity Ch 6: Pressure, Winds, Storms and Cyclones

objectives: I can define pressure as the force acting per unit area.
I can calculate pressure using pressure = force ÷ area, in N/cm² or N/m² (pascal).
I can explain everyday designs that increase or reduce pressure.
misconceptions: Pressure and force are the same thing.
A bigger force always means a bigger pressure (area matters too).
Sharp objects cut because they are stronger.
